question: How do fee-bump transactions and channel or fee-paying accounts work, does the fee account sign or use sequence, why can fees look doubled, and what is the fee pool?

golden.answer: A fee-bump wraps a signed inner transaction. The outer fee source signs and pays; the inner source, sequence and signatures stay authoritative and the fee source's own sequence is not used. The outer fee is one total bid for inner operations plus one, charged once, so inner and outer fee fields do not add. Channel accounts are separate source accounts whose sequence lanes give parallel throughput. Fees go to the fee pool, not validators.
keyFacts: The fee source signs and pays; the inner source, sequence and signatures stay unchanged.
The charged outer fee and the inner fee field are not additive.
Channel accounts are separate transaction sources giving sequence-number lanes.
avoid: Do NOT say a fee-bump replaces inner authorization, consumes the fee source sequence, or doubles the fee.
golden.notes: Either the XDR total-bid or the SDK per-operation baseFee description is correct if consistent.

GT-29 CORRECTION 2026-07-10: displayed inner/outer fee fields are not additive charges; the fee source incurs the outer charged fee.
Fee layers: XDR FeeBumpTransaction.fee is the total bid. The docs 'Fee' attribute and the js-stellar-base buildFeeBumpTransaction baseFee are a per-operation bid multiplied by inner operations + 1 (js-stellar-base also adds the inner Soroban resource fee). An answer that describes either layer correctly is not wrong.
